section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Complex Plane
section_1.content: Introduce the complex plane where the horizontal axis represents real numbers and the vertical axis represents imaginary numbers (i).
section_1.example: Visualizing a character moving on a 2D map: X-axis (Real) and Y-axis (Imaginary). A point 3+2i is just '3 units right, 2 units up'.

section_2.title: The Meaning of i and Rotation
section_2.content: Explain that multiplying by 'i' performs a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation. Repeated multiplication creates circular motion.
section_2.example: An animation of a robotic arm rotating 90 degrees every time it gets 'multiplied' by i.

section_3.title: Introducing the Taylor Series (The Engine)
section_3.content: Briefly introduce the concept that complex functions can be expressed as infinite sums (Taylor Series) of simpler terms (powers).
section_3.example: A 'building block' metaphor: Showing how stacking simple rectangles (polynomials) can eventually trace out a smooth sine wave.

section_4.title: The Euler Identity Derivation
section_4.content: Connect the series expansions of e^x, cos(x), and sin(x). Show how e^(ix) combines into a circular path on the complex plane: cos(x) + i*sin(x).
section_4.example: A visual 'mesh' merging the graphs of sin/cos and e^x to show they overlap perfectly when i is introduced.

section_5.title: The Grand Finale: e^(πi) = -1
section_5.content: Set x = π. Show how the rotation on the unit circle lands exactly at -1 on the real axis.
section_5.example: A 'Point-Runner' animation: A character starts at 1, travels along the arc of a circle for a distance of π radians, and stops exactly at -1.
